headline: The relief lasted one session: the dollar is back at a 52-week high and crude is up 5.8% on the week, while the selling rotated out of chips and into banks, machinery and healthcare.
summary: Yesterday's two-day truce in the dollar and the barrel is gone. DXY is +0.4% to 102.58, z=1.75 with acceleration 1.66 and the 100th percentile of 52 weeks; EURUSD sits at 1.1201, the 5th percentile; USDMXN is 18.37, +8.2% on the month at z=3.05 with acceleration 2.07, still the most extreme print in the book. Crude took the week back: WTI +0.9% on the day and +5.8% on the week to 94.60, Brent +5.5% to 106.16, natural gas +4.8% on the day and +17.2% on the month, and XLE led every sector at +1.8%. The one genuine improvement is duration — after Williams pushed back on 2027 hikes, 10s fell 3bp to 5.21%, 30s 4bp to 5.56%, the 10-year real yield 3bp to 2.88%, and the rates composite improved to -64 from -74 with the regime at -7 versus -12. But tightening did not stop; it moved venue. It is now coming through FX and energy, not the curve, and breakevens at 2.33% give CPI no cushion.

The damage also changed address. Day one of bank earnings was a mark-down: XLF -0.4%, BX -4.2% on the session and -14.4% on the month (z=-1.51), GS -13.3% on the month at z=-1.91, KBE -7.0%, KRE -6.0% with KRE/SPY at the 14th percentile, IAI -6.5%, JPM -6.5%. Heavy machinery joined: CAT -3.3% on the day and -10.5% on the week. Health care was the day's worst sector at -1.4%, with XBI -3.0% and IBB -2.1%. None of this shows up in the index because the index is not the market: SPX 7807 at the 99th percentile, 7.6% above its 200-day, while IWM/SPY is z=-1.61 at the 9th percentile and RSP/SPY at the 12th. Breadth composite -17.

Inside tech, the de-rating of silicon continued and stayed geographically contained. SOXX -7.7% and SMH -7.0% on the week, MU -8.8%, TSM -7.7%, ASML -6.3%, EWY -10.6% with z=-1.51 and acceleration -1.53, KOSPI -8.8% on the week. Taiwan did not break: TWII +6.7% on the month at the 98th percentile with relative strength up, EWT +2.3%. The money stayed in the same theme one layer up — IGV/SMH +7.4% in a week and +21.0% over three months, CIBR +13.8% on the month with acceleration z=2.01, PLTR +24.8%, META +17.8% and +2.6% today, MSFT +9.6% and at the 100th percentile, AMD +1.9%. ORCL bounced 4.2% off a -52.9% year. The picks-and-shovels leg keeps collapsing: REMX -18.6% on the month at the 0th percentile and 33% below its 200-day, NLR -12.2% at the 0th, uranium -14.1%; electrons still get paid, with VST +9.6% on the month and GEV +4.9%.

Hedges are the cheapest thing on the screen and the hedge assets themselves are being liquidated. VIX 15.21 at the 10th percentile, VIX3M 17.93 at the 4th, SKEW 155 at the 81st — while MOVE is back above 100 (+2.7% on the day, +23.0% on the month, z=1.19). Gold is -5.1% on the month at z=-1.31 and in a downtrend, silver -8.1%, GDX -10.2% with relative strength -12.0% and GDX/gold acceleration z=-1.57, yet copper is +4.0% at the 96th percentile and copper/gold is at the 100th percentile with z=1.38. That mix says growth, not stress — which is flatly at odds with transports (IYT/SPY 6th percentile), housing (30-year mortgage 7.40%, z=2.06, acceleration 1.50, 100th percentile; ITB and XHB/SPY at the 2nd and 1st percentiles) and the bank tape. Credit is the one thing still refusing to confirm: HYG/IEF at the 89th percentile, BKLN at the 91st, credit composite 41, though HYG is now rolling over at z=-1.01.

good.text: Duration caught a bid on dovish Fed commentary: 10s -3bp to 5.21%, 30s -4bp to 5.56%, 10-year real yield -3bp to 2.88%. Rates composite improved to -64 from -74 and the risk regime to -7 from -12.
Credit still will not crack. HYG/IEF at the 89th percentile, BKLN at the 91st and flat on the day, LQD -0.0%, credit composite +41. Nothing systemic is being priced.

Energy is the cleanest trend in the book: XLE +1.8% on the day and +5.4% on the week at the 100th percentile, XOP +2.8% / +6.0%, XOM +1.1% at a 52-week high, CVX +1.3%. Relative strength +1.7%/+14.4%.

The cyclical metal is confirming growth even as the safe-haven metal fails: copper +0.5% on the day and +4.0% on the month at the 96th percentile, copper/gold at the 100th percentile with z=1.38 and acceleration 1.04.

AI leadership rotated rather than broke. CIBR +13.8% on the month with acceleration z=2.01, IGV +9.3% and relative strength +7.1%/+14.3%, PLTR +24.8%, META +17.8%, MSFT +9.6% at the 100th percentile, AMD +17.3%.
Crypto keeps repairing: BTC +1.8% to 83,205, ETH +2.2%, SOL +1.0%, all reading turning_up, MSTR +16.2% on the month and IBIT +7.7%.

bad.text: The dollar reclaimed the high: DXY +0.4% to 102.58, z=1.75, acceleration 1.66, 100th percentile. EURUSD at the 5th percentile, USDMXN z=3.05 with acceleration 2.07, USDKRW acceleration 1.41. EM relative is rolling over hard — EEM/SPY z=-1.21 with acceleration -1.51.

Crude took back the whole relief trade: WTI +5.8% and Brent +5.5% on the week, natgas +17.2% on the month, DBC at the 98th percentile — an inflation impulse landing into a CPI print with 10-year breakevens still pinned at 2.33%.

Financials are being marked down in real time on day one of earnings: BX -4.2%, GS -13.3% on the month at z=-1.91, KBE -7.0%, KRE -6.0%, IAI -6.5%, JPM -6.5%, with 2s10s rolling over 6bp on the week to 42bp.

The memory/Korea de-rating is accelerating downward: EWY -10.6% on the week at z=-1.51 with acceleration -1.53, KOSPI -8.8%, SOXX -7.7%, MU -8.8%, TSM -7.7%. Taiwan is not following — this is a specific unwind, not a sector top yet.

Housing is the unpriced structural break: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +69bp on the month, z=2.06 with acceleration 1.50 at the 100th percentile; ITB -4.7% on the month and 11.8% below its 200-day, XHB/SPY at the 1st percentile.

Equity vol is priced for nothing while bond vol rebuilds: VIX 15.21 (10th percentile) and VIX3M 17.93 (4th) against MOVE back over 100, +23.0% on the month at z=1.19 — with breadth at IWM/SPY 9th percentile and RSP/SPY 12th.

trades.name: Long XOP / short JETS
trades.line: Long XOP vs short JETS: crude back up 5.8% on the week
trades.expr: Equal-dollar pair: long XOP, short JETS. Size 1.0x/1.0x; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: Crude round-tripped the entire relief move while the fuel-consumer complex is already in a downtrend. Producers are at new highs with the best relative strength in the book; airlines are the purest short-side expression of a $95 barrel.
trades.trigger: WTI +5.8% on the week to 94.60 and Brent +5.5% to 106.16; XLE led all sectors at +1.8% and XOP +2.8% on the day at the 100th percentile. JETS -4.6% on the week, -13.1% over three months, relative strength -6.8%/-16.3%.
trades.stop: WTI closing below 88 or the pair down 7%. WTI's 1-month acceleration is already -1.64 and RBOB fell 4.8% today — a crack-spread-led break in product would invalidate.

trades.name: Short regional banks (KRE)
trades.line: Short KRE into earnings: KRE/SPY at the 14th percentile
trades.expr: Short KRE outright, or buy Dec 68/60 put spreads; hedge beta with a half-size SPY long if you want the pure relative.
trades.thesis: Banks go into earnings already marked down, the curve is flattening again rather than steepening into their margins, and the alt/broker complex is breaking first — the classic sequence before credit-sensitive lenders get repriced.
trades.trigger: Day one of earnings: XLF -0.4%, BX -4.2%, GS -13.3% on the month at z=-1.91, KBE -7.0% at z=-1.08, KRE -6.0% with KRE/SPY z=-1.06 at the 14th percentile. 2s10s -6bp on the week to 42bp, and HYG is now rolling over at z=-1.01.
trades.stop: KRE back above 72 with KRE/SPY reclaiming 0.095, or 2s10s steepening above 60bp while HYG/IEF makes a new high.

trades.name: Long IGV / short SMH
trades.line: Software over silicon: IGV/SMH +7.4% in a week, +21% in 3m
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, equal dollars. Add CIBR as a 25% overlay on the long leg.
trades.thesis: Capital is rotating within AI, not out of it. Hardware is de-rating on Asian supply-chain stress while software and security monetization accelerates — the ratio is trending with the strongest acceleration in the industry book.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +7.4% on the week, +5.7% on the month, +21.0% over three months; IGV +9.3% on the month with relative strength +7.1%/+14.3% and CIBR acceleration z=2.01. Against it: SOXX -7.7% on the week, MU -8.8%, TSM -7.7%, EWY -10.6% at acceleration z=-1.53.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.178, or SOXX up more than 6% in a week with EWY and KOSPI reversing their weekly losses.

trades.name: Short home construction (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB on today's bounce: mortgage 7.40%, z=2.06
trades.expr: Short ITB into today's +0.8% bounce, or buy Jan 84/74 put spreads. Pair against a half-size SPY long if you want it market-neutral.
trades.thesis: A 69bp one-month jump in the 30-year mortgage to 7.40% has not been earned back by the 3bp rally in 10s. Builder margins and order books get hit with a lag the index has not discounted; the group is already at the lows and still bouncing on headlines, giving a clean entry.
trades.trigger: MORTGAGE30US 7.40%, z=2.06 with acceleration 1.50, 100th percentile of 52 weeks; ITB +0.8% and XHB +0.6% today after -4.7%/-3.4% months, ITB 11.8% below its 200-day, XHB/SPY at the 1st percentile; HD -4.8% on the month, DHI -1.8%.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage below 7.00% or ITB closing above 92 (+8%).

trades.name: Long index convexity (SPY puts / VIX calls)
trades.line: Buy Dec convexity: VIX3M at the 4th percentile vs MOVE 101
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPY 5% OTM puts financed by selling 8% OTM puts (1x2 avoided), plus a Dec VIX 20/30 call spread for 0.25-0.35% of NAV total.
trades.thesis: The index sits at the 99th percentile on narrowing participation while bond vol has rebuilt above 100 and the dollar is at a 52-week high. Equity vol is the cheapest asset in the book relative to the macro it is supposed to insure.
trades.trigger: VIX 15.21 at the 10th percentile and VIX3M 17.93 at the 4th, with VIX term structure turning up and SKEW 155 at the 81st percentile; MOVE +2.7% today, +23.0% on the month at z=1.19; IWM/SPY 9th percentile, RSP/SPY 12th; SPX 7.6% above its 200-day.
trades.stop: Hard premium cap of 35bp of NAV. Thesis is wrong if RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY recover their 1-month highs while MOVE falls back under 90.
trades.target: VIX 22-25 / SPX -5%; 3-4x on the call spread.

trades.name: Long EWZ / short EWW
trades.line: Brazil over Mexico: USDMXN z=3.05 vs USDBRL -2.3% 1m
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal dollars. Express the FX leg separately only if you can hold a short MXN carry cost.
trades.thesis: EM is dispersing, not de-rating. Brazil has the trend, the currency and the relative strength; Mexico has the single most stressed FX reading in the book and an equity market rolling over with it.
trades.trigger: EWZ +12.3% on the month at z=1.37 with relative strength +10.0%, BVSP at the 97th percentile, USDBRL -2.3% on the month. Against it: USDMXN 18.37, +8.2% on the month at z=3.05 with acceleration 2.07, EWW -2.8% on the month and rolling over.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.60 while USDBRL breaks 5.15, or the pair down 7%.

trades.name: Long FCX / short GDX
trades.line: Long copper equity vs short gold miners: Cu/Au 100th pctile
trades.expr: Long FCX (add COPX for breadth), short GDX, equal dollars.
trades.thesis: Copper/gold at the 100th percentile with the metal at the 96th while the precious complex is in an outright downtrend. Gold miners carry the most negative acceleration in the industry book and are losing to their own underlying.
trades.trigger: Copper +0.5% today, +4.0% on the month; CU_AU z=1.38 with acceleration 1.04 at the 100th percentile. Gold -5.1% on the month at z=-1.31 in a downtrend, GDX -10.2% with relative strength -12.0% and acceleration -1.16, GDX/gold acceleration z=-1.57, silver -8.1%.
trades.stop: Gold reclaiming 4400 with GDX/gold turning up, or copper/gold falling back 8% from here; pair stop -7%.
